scope: Search-engine result pages treated as canonical: keep only parameters that change which results are shown.
method: Read-only. Primary sources: Ecosia iOS browser and live Ecosia web bundle; Qwant live front-end bundle and Qwant API filter definitions; SearXNG source (webadapter.py, webapp.py, preferences.py, templates). Cross-checked against openserp, SearXNG's Qwant engine, Firefox search-config-v2, OpenSearch descriptions, ClearURLs and AdGuard TrackParamFilter (neither has Ecosia or SearXNG rules; AdGuard only covers lite.qwant.com/redirect/).

engines.path_notes: Verticals /search, /images, /news and /videos come from Ecosia's own iOS browser (EcosiaSearchVertical enum). /shopping is listed in Ecosia's help (#s shortcut) and appears as a tab link in a captured 2026 SERP. /ai-chat also takes q (plus origin=) but is an AI chat page, not a result page; treat it as q-only if handled at all. Staging hosts ecosia-staging.xyz and ecosia-dev.xyz exist in Ecosia's Android code and should be ignored.

functional.condition: Internal QA parameter; kept only because it changes results

engines.settings_not_in_url: Search region (market), SafeSearch and interface language are NOT URL parameters on Ecosia: they live in the ECFG cookie (mc = market, f = adult filter, l = language, c = country). The region filter writes the cookie and reloads the same URL minus p. A cleaned Ecosia link therefore cannot preserve region or SafeSearch; only forceMarket (internal) touches the market via the URL. Sources: https://github.com/ecosia/ios-browser/blob/main/firefox-ios/Ecosia/Core/Cookie/MainCookieHandler.swift ; https://www.ecosia.org/static/images/assets/chunks/chunk-Bbtlr4qS.js ; https://www.ecosia.org/static/images/assets/entries/src_pages_images.DQLfWBII.js ; https://github.com/karust/openserp/blob/HEAD/ecosia/url.go
engines.notes: Primary evidence is Ecosia's own code: the iOS browser (EcosiaQueryItemName: ar, p, q, test, tt, _sp) and the live web bundle fetched 2026-10-10, whose search form keeps exactly these parameters on a new search: freshness, resolution, videoLength, size, color, imageType, aspect, license, plus canary, mocked, forceProvider, sfs, sfn, forceMarket, tt, tts, addon, addonversion. Image filter values are hard-coded in that bundle. openserp (active Go scraper, 2026-09) independently confirms method=index, q, freshness, p and imageType. Bundle file names are content-hashed and will rotate; the parameter names were stable across python-ecosia-images (2019: size, color, imageType, freshness, license) and the 2026 bundle. Recommended rule: allowlist q, p, freshness everywhere; add size, color, imageType, aspect, license, offset on /images; videoLength, resolution on /videos; keep forceMarket/forceProvider if present; drop everything else. Parameter names are case-sensitive (imageType, videoLength).
engines.test_notes: videoLength=short is an illustrative value; the rule keys on the parameter name only.

engines.path_notes: Every Qwant vertical is served from the root path; the vertical is chosen by t. lite.qwant.com/?q=bergen&t=web redirected to www.qwant.com/?q=bergen&t=web when tested on 2026-10-10, and SearXNG dropped its Qwant Lite engine on 2026-05-25, so lite links are legacy (lite used p for pages). lite.qwant.com/redirect/ is a click-out redirector, not a result page. www.qwantjunior.com is listed in Firefox's search config. qwant.com/maps/ is a separate map app and out of scope.

engines.notes: Primary evidence is Qwant's own front-end code fetched 2026-10-10: the URL-parameter enum (q, t, o, sticky, l, locale, video, count, offset, device, u, source, origin, client, cl, f, tgp, chrome_dse_attribution, fs, imagetype, license, size, color, filters, guid, safesearch, s, freshness, age, order, home, homecard, eval, category, nocache, _feature, campaign, account, llm, llm_force, sr, r, cw_creative, cw_features, externalsource, site, distribution, survey, entry_point) and the per-vertical allow-lists that decide which URL parameters reach the API: base [q, tgp, locale, origin, distribution]; images [t, color, freshness, imagetype, license, size, source]; news [t, u, source, freshness, order]; videos [t, order, source]; shopping [t, order, filters, guid, page, filter[...]]; web [offset, device, safesearch, freshness, age]. The settings hook reads each setting (theme, hc, hti, hb, b, s, l, locale, home, hometab, cl, omnibar, llm) from the URL first. Filter value lists are delivered by the API (result.filters) and change by vertical and market; the web and images API returned DataDome 403 from this network, so their value lists were not captured. Bundle file names are content-hashed and will rotate. Recommended rule: keep q, t, locale, l, s, safesearch, sr+r, freshness, order, source, size, color, imagetype, license, u, offset, filters, filter[...], page, guid, age, category, and p on lite.qwant.com; drop the rest.
engines.test_notes: Image filter values in test 2 are illustrative (Qwant serves them from the API); the rule keys on names.

hosts: * (any host: self-hosted; 94 public instances on searx.space as of 2026-10-10)
engines.path_notes: Both / and /search accept GET and POST; / with a q parameter answers 308 to /search with the same query string (verified on a private instance on 2026-10-10). An instance can live under a path prefix (settings server.base_url), so match a path ending in /search, or the instance root, rather than an exact path. Hosts are arbitrary, so detection must combine path and parameters (see detection).

detection.known_hosts: a private instance used for the checks (its names are left out of this copy), plus the searx.space list https://searx.space/data/instances.json
detection.rule: Treat a URL as a SearXNG result page when q is present, the path is /search or the root (optionally under a prefix), and at least one SearXNG-specific parameter is present: pageno, time_range, category_<name>, engine_data-<engine>-<key>, timeout_limit, engines, or categories together with language or safesearch. pageno and category_* are the strongest single signals (Google uses start, Bing first, DuckDuckGo s). On a known host, q alone is enough.
detection.caution: categories, language, safesearch, format and theme are generic names used by other sites; do not fire on them alone.

functional.name: q
functional.meaning: Search query. Carries SearXNG bang and modifier syntax (!engine, !!bang, :language, <timeout) inside the value.

functional.name: pageno
functional.meaning: Page number, one-based integer (default 1).

functional.name: categories
functional.meaning: Comma-separated category list (general, images, videos, news, map, music, it, science, files, social media, plus any instance-defined category).

functional.name: category_<name>
functional.meaning: Alternative per-category switch used by the HTML forms (category_images=1; value 'off' removes it). Names can contain spaces (category_social+media).

functional.name: engines
functional.meaning: Comma-separated explicit engine list; combined with any categories given.

functional.name: language
functional.meaning: Search language: all, auto, or a code such as en or en-GB.

functional.name: safesearch
functional.meaning: 0 none, 1 moderate, 2 strict.

functional.name: time_range
functional.meaning: day, week, month, year (empty or None means none). The API doc lists day, month, year; the code also accepts week.

functional.name: timeout_limit
functional.meaning: Per-search engine timeout in seconds; changes which engines answer in time. SearXNG includes it in its own 'Search URL' box.

functional.name: format
functional.meaning: Output format: html (default), json, csv, rss. Changes the returned resource (feed or API) rather than the result set; non-html formats return 403 unless enabled.

functional.name: engine_data-<engine>-<key>
functional.meaning: Engine pagination state (cursors/next-page tokens) echoed by the results form, used by e.g. piped, youtube_noapi, pinterest, deviantart.

functional.name: enabled_engines
functional.meaning: Preference override parsed from GET: engines to enable for this request.

functional.name: disabled_engines
functional.meaning: Preference override parsed from GET: engines to disable for this request.

functional.name: locale
functional.meaning: Interface (UI translation) language. Does not change results; kept only because interface language counts as functional in this spec.
functional.condition: Interface only; drop if CheckLink decides UI language is not canonical

nonfunctional.name: theme
nonfunctional.meaning: UI theme (simple). The HTML search form always adds it, so it appears in most copied SearXNG URLs.

nonfunctional.name: preferences
nonfunctional.meaning: Base64 zlib blob of the sharer's whole preference set (engines, plugins, tokens, UI). Personal settings and possibly secrets; the explicit parameters already carry result-affecting state.

nonfunctional.name: tokens
nonfunctional.meaning: Access tokens that unlock private engines. A secret: always remove.

nonfunctional.name: enabled_plugins
nonfunctional.meaning: Plugin toggles (answers, URL rewriting); personal settings.
nonfunctional.confidence: judgement: some plugins alter answers, not the engine result set

nonfunctional.name: disabled_plugins
nonfunctional.meaning: As enabled_plugins.

nonfunctional.name: autocomplete
nonfunctional.meaning: Autocomplete backend.

nonfunctional.name: favicon_resolver
nonfunctional.meaning: Favicon source.

nonfunctional.name: image_proxy
nonfunctional.meaning: Proxy result images.

nonfunctional.name: method
nonfunctional.meaning: Form submission method preference (GET/POST).

nonfunctional.name: results_on_new_tab
nonfunctional.meaning: Open results in a new tab.

nonfunctional.name: doi_resolver
nonfunctional.meaning: DOI link resolver for the open-access rewrite plugin.

nonfunctional.name: simple_style
nonfunctional.meaning: Light/dark/black style of the simple theme.

nonfunctional.name: center_alignment
nonfunctional.meaning: Layout preference.

nonfunctional.name: query_in_title
nonfunctional.meaning: Put the query in the page title.

nonfunctional.name: search_on_category_select
nonfunctional.meaning: Search immediately on category click.

nonfunctional.name: hotkeys
nonfunctional.meaning: Keyboard shortcut scheme (default, vim).

nonfunctional.name: url_formatting
nonfunctional.meaning: How result URLs are displayed (pretty, full, host).

engines.notes: SearXNG merges GET and POST into one form, applies every recognised preference key from it, then builds the search from q, pageno, safesearch, time_range, timeout_limit, language, categories/category_*, engines and engine_data-*. Its own canonical 'Search URL' box (search_url.html) is q, language, time_range, safesearch, pageno (only when > 1), categories, timeout_limit, which matches this allowlist; CheckLink may additionally drop empty values (time_range= is emitted empty by SearXNG itself). Unknown parameters are ignored by SearXNG, so utm_* and similar are safe to strip. Source code read at commit f4822b3 (2026-10-09); the private instance used for the checks runs 9f042d2 (2026.10.9).
engines.test_notes: Test 2 keeps the root path (CheckLink removes parameters, it does not rewrite /?q= to /search). Test 3 uses a searx.space instance to show host-agnostic detection (pageno is absent, but format plus q on /search on a listed host qualifies; on an unknown host the rule needs a stronger signal).
